Canonical research core · lean

Conditional forward-freeze exchange and lag-eight restriction

Constructs unique exchange witnesses from an actual forward-freeze collision. In the stated lag-eight seven-host schedule and row window, a collision can only occur at row q and freeze at q+1 or q+2.

Lean verified (stated scope)

Verification applies only to the recorded source snapshot and check scope. Consult the coverage report for build and axiom-check details.

Scientific review

Review verdict: passed. Evidence and exact scope are linked above.

Hypotheses and scope

  • The exchange retains all host/freeze equalities and strict index inequalities. The lag-eight theorem requires q>=26, Lag8TargetSevenHostSchedule q g host, q-4<=t<=q+2, c=host(t), c<k, gameF(k,c)=k and k<q+3.

Formalization correspondence

The companion witness lies below c, equals k in row t, and is unique by row injectivity. The full exchange additionally reconstructs v at row k left of its original victim. The specialized schedule theorem rules out all but its two dynamic rows only after the supplied schedule is unfolded.

Verification evidence

This corrected source snapshot passed a new clean strict build, exhaustive serialized and elaborated declaration/axiom census, and five fresh Lean kernel replays. Exact source/type correspondence and unchanged logical declarations after the documented comment corrections were checked separately. Only the standard propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound axioms were observed. Module and compiler-declaration counts are not counts of independent mathematical theorems.
